steps.claim: Mount Tambora erupts (VEI 7)

test.source: eruption peaked 10 Apr 1815; ice-core sulfate records

steps.claim: The Year Without a Summer: crops fail

test.source: 1816 cold anomaly and harvest failures across Europe and New England; tree-ring and temperature records

steps.link_why: the cooling is attributed to Tambora's sulfate aerosols in the climate literature

steps.claim: Oat prices soar; horses starve or are slaughtered

test.reason: grain prices did spike in 1816–17; the scale of horse losses and the '300%' oat figure lack a clear primary source

steps.claim: Karl Drais rides the first two-wheeler

test.source: Drais's first ride, Mannheim, 12 Jun 1817

steps.note: The horse-shortage motive is historian Hans-Erhard Lessing's hypothesis; Drais's 1818 privilege does not state it.

steps.claim: Pedals and cranks make the modern bicycle

test.source: Michaux and Lallement add pedals to the front wheel, 1860s (Lallement's US patent, 1866)

steps.link_why: the pedal velocipede is a direct descendant of Drais's two-wheel design

title: A failed quinine experiment and chemotherapy (1856)

steps.claim: Perkin makes mauveine while chasing synthetic quinine

test.source: William Perkin's discovery, Easter 1856; patent Aug 1856

steps.claim: A synthetic dye industry takes off

test.source: German and British coal-tar dye firms grow through the 1860s–1880s (BASF 1865, Hoechst 1863)

steps.link_why: the industry grew directly from Perkin's mauveine

steps.claim: Ehrlich finds dyes stain microbes selectively

test.source: Paul Ehrlich's staining work, 1870s–1882 (staining of the tuberculosis bacillus)

steps.link_why: Ehrlich used the new synthetic dyes

steps.claim: Ehrlich's lab finds Salvarsan, the first 'magic bullet'

test.source: Salvarsan (arsphenamine) identified by Sahachiro Hata in Ehrlich's lab, 1909

steps.note: Salvarsan is an arsenic compound; the selective-targeting idea came from dye staining.
steps.link_why: Ehrlich credited selective dye staining with his targeted-therapy idea

steps.claim: Targeted chemicals become cancer chemotherapy

test.source: nitrogen mustard results published 1946 (Goodman, Gilman and colleagues)

steps.note: Modern cancer chemotherapy grew mainly from WWII nitrogen-mustard research; Ehrlich's 'chemotherapy' idea is an ancestor, not the direct source.

title: Wartime radar and the microwave oven (1940)

steps.claim: Randall and Boot build the cavity magnetron

test.source: University of Birmingham, first operated 21 Feb 1940

steps.claim: A candy bar melts in Percy Spencer's pocket

test.source: Spencer's account of the melted candy bar at Raytheon, 1945

steps.link_why: Spencer worked on Raytheon's magnetron production

steps.claim: Popcorn and an egg confirm microwave cooking

test.source: Spencer's popcorn and egg tests, 1945 (Raytheon history)

steps.claim: Raytheon patents microwave cooking; the Radarange launches

test.source: patent filed 8 Oct 1945 (US 2,495,429); the Radarange, about 750 lb, sold from 1947

steps.link_why: Raytheon built it from its magnetron business

steps.claim: Amana's countertop Radarange reaches homes at $495

test.source: Amana (a Raytheon subsidiary) countertop Radarange, 1967, $495

steps.link_why: Raytheon bought Amana to bring the Radarange to homes

title: The 1906 earthquake and Bank of America (1906)

steps.claim: The earthquake and fires destroy San Francisco's financial district

test.source: earthquake 18 Apr 1906; fires for three days

steps.claim: Giannini rescues his bank's cash in produce wagons

test.source: A.P. Giannini moves about $80,000 from the Bank of Italy, 18 Apr 1906 (Bank of America history)

steps.link_why: the rescue was a direct response to the fire

steps.claim: He lends from a plank on the waterfront

test.source: Giannini lends from a plank across two barrels at the North Beach wharf, days after the fire

steps.link_why: other banks' vaults were too hot to open

steps.claim: The Bank of Italy pioneers branch banking

test.source: first branch outside San Francisco, San Jose, 1909

steps.link_why: histories credit the post-quake loyalty and deposits

steps.claim: It becomes Bank of America

test.source: renamed Bank of America, 1930; the largest commercial bank in the world by 1945

steps.note: Largest in the US by the 1940s, not in 1930.

steps.claim: Sputnik 1 launches, beeping at 20.005 and 40.002 MHz

test.source: launch 4 Oct 1957

steps.claim: Guier and Weiffenbach track its Doppler shift

test.source: Johns Hopkins APL, days after launch (APL Technical Digest history)

steps.claim: They compute its full orbit from one ground station

test.source: orbit determination from Doppler data, early 1958, on a UNIVAC

steps.link_why: the method used their Sputnik recordings

steps.claim: McClure inverts the math: a known orbit locates the receiver

test.source: Frank McClure's proposal, March 1958

steps.claim: The Navy's Transit system works; GPS follows

test.source: Transit 1B, first successful launch 13 Apr 1960; GPS development from 1973

steps.link_why: Transit was built on the Doppler method; GPS succeeded it
